title: PH, South Korea eye deeper climate, environmental ties
summary: The comedians are ready for another round of laughter and challenges in the second season of “LOL: Last One Laughing Philippines,” as the official trailer gives a glimpse of the upcoming competition.

blocks.text: The Philippines and South Korea are seeking to strengthen their partnership to boost environmental governance and climate resilience in Southeast Asia.

The talks between Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna and South Korean South Korean Ambassador and Deputy Minister for Climate Change Jongho Kyun were made on the sidelines of the 81st Session of the UN General Assembly High-Level Week and Climate Week NYC 2026.

“As we move toward COP31, we see the priority increasingly shifting from commitments to implementation and delivery—translating climate goals into policies, investments, technologies, and measurable outcomes,” said Cuna in a statement.

COP31 or the 31st Conference of Parties, is the United Nations Climate Change Conference, where parties to the convention decide and negotiate on how to solve the climate crisis. This year's COP will take place in Turkiye in November.
Both Manila and Seoul acknowledge the need for countries that are at risk from climate-related hazards to access the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage (FRLD).
The Philippines is host to the board of the FRLD.

“There is a need to establish practical pathways so that countries most vulnerable to climate impacts can access support when loss and damage occur,” said Cuna. “The FRLD can play an important role in helping countries recover, rebuild, and strengthen resilience.”

The DENR chief thanked South Korea for its support through the Korea International Cooperation Agency, highlighting initiatives to cut marine plastic waste, emergency assistance during the Mindoro oil spill, and the recent assignment of the specialized cleanup ship MV Nilad to Manila Bay.

To formalize and broaden their collaboration, both countries are fast-tracking talks on two key pacts: a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) on Environmental Cooperation and another on Climate Change Cooperation. Environment Secretary Cuna stated that both parties plan to finalize the agreements before the bilateral summit at the 49th ASEAN Summit in Manila this November 2026, which the Philippines is hosting.

According to Cuna, the upcoming MOUs will target joint initiatives on Article 6 Paris Agreement carbon markets, emissions reduction, water resource management, and ecosystem-based disaster risk mitigation. — LA, GMA News
